newsitem.title: FRANCE: France praises Turkish law reform, seeks EU ties.
newsitem.headline: France praises Turkish law reform, seeks EU ties.

text.p: France praised a new Turkish detention law on Wednesday and said continuous human rights improvements should help closer ties with the European Union.
The new law shortens the maximum term of police detention from 30 to 10 days in nine provinces under emergency rule and from 14 to seven days in the rest of the country.
But the human rights group Amnesty International said it was insufficient and unlikely to prevent torture.

"We are pleased with the adoption by the Turkish National Assembly of a law reducing the duration of police custody," the French Foreign Ministry said, noting it kept a pledge made to EU countries by Turkish Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller.

"We encourage the Turkish authorities to continue on this path. A series of measures guaranteeing freedom of expression has also been announced and should soon be the subject of legislation," it said in a statement.
"Improvement of the human rights situation must be a continuous process as is the rapprochement which we strongly wish between Turkey and the European Union," it added.

The comment appeared to be an indirect criticism of a statement made after six EU centrist and Christian Democratic leaders, including German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, met last week, that Turkey had no prospect of ever joining the Union.

French European Affairs Minister Michel Barnier criticised that view on Monday, saying it was vital for European stability that Turkey retain a "European prospect", even if EU membership was not realistic in the short term.

The United States has sent a special envoy on Greek-Turkish affairs to Europe this week to urge EU countries not to slam the door on Turkey, as well as discussing efforts to resolve the Cyprus conflict.
